findings.issue: The new expansive-depth frontier has no advisor reach. Probes authored from the feature before reading advisor metadata (probes-pre-metadata.md #2 and #5) fail: 'Investigate iteratively why the parser drops unicode and keep a depth-capped frontier of follow-up questions' returns zero recommendations, and 'Audit this spec folder for release readiness and keep a frontier of sub-targets open until they are exhausted' ranks system-spec-kit above system-deep-loop. A natural request naming the feature ('Research token refresh in expansive depth mode') also returns zero recommendations, and the completed-run extension wording ('Extend the completed review run by three iterations') ranks sk-code first. Cause: neither mode's `aliases` nor its `advisorRouting.legacyAliases` carries the feature vocabulary, and the hub's description/keyword surfaces omit it, so the advisor projection cannot score the feature. Add mode-specific feature phrases (research: 'depth-capped frontier', 'frontier of follow-up questions'; review: 'expansive depth review', 'frontier of sub-targets') to the registry aliases and legacy aliases, keep hub-router.json and ROUTER.md INTENT_SIGNALS in sync, update the projection maps so the drift guard passes, and replay each new phrase against an out-of-domain prompt. Do not add a bare 'frontier' to both modes: it ties and the tieBreak silently picks research.

findings.issue: The new `depth_mode` flag is described in the PRE-BOUND schema (line 190) and the Default Resolution Table (line 215), but the `:auto` Tier-1 persist shape at line 162 still lists `antiConvergence.convergenceMode` and omits `antiConvergence.depthMode`; the review contract has the same omission at line 156. A run following the contract's own Tier-1 shape writes a config without the flag and only gets it back when the YAML's `step_create_config` rewrites the file, so the command contract is internally inconsistent. Add `antiConvergence.depthMode` to the shape in both presentation sources (`.skilled/commands/deep/assets/deep-research-presentation.txt` and `deep-review-presentation.txt`) and regenerate with `compile-command-contracts.cjs --command deep/research --write` and `--command deep/review --write`; do not hand-edit the generated contract.

The S9-command-references battery row fails on a runtime data path, not on a broken deep command reference. `.skilled/commands/speckit/assets/speckit-resume.yaml:104` names `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/database/access-telemetry.json`; `.gitignore:431` ignores that whole directory, so a clean checkout never holds it. The validator already exempts `.skilled/skills/.state/` (line 131) and the deep-loop sqlite databases (line 134), but not this gitignored runtime database. The four S9 scope files resolve cleanly: a scoped run over both deep YAMLs exits 0. Extend the runtime-artifact exemption (ideally derive it from the gitignore roots) so the check is green in a fresh checkout.
